import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
from scipy import stats

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

START, END = "20181201", "20251231"
CODES = ["000300.SH", "000852.SH", "000905.SH"]
ROLE = {"000300.SH": "A", "000852.SH": "B", "000905.SH": "C"}
LABEL = {"000300.SH": "A = 000300.SH", "000852.SH": "B = 000852.SH", "000905.SH": "C = 000905.SH"}
WIN = 12

grid = pd.period_range("2018-12", "2025-12", freq="M")          # 85 months
analysis = grid[grid >= pd.Period("2019-01", freq="M")]          # 84 months
mask_pre = analysis[analysis <= pd.Period("2022-12", freq="M")]
mask_post = analysis[analysis >= pd.Period("2023-01", freq="M")]

def finite_or_none(v):
    if v is None:
        return None
    v = float(v)
    return v if np.isfinite(v) else None

# ---- load month-end levels (level transform, no filling) -------------------
levels, measure_used = {}, {}
for code in CODES:
    got = None
    for measure in ("market.cny_close", "market.adjusted_close"):
        try:
            df = data.series("index", code, start=START, end=END, measure=measure,
                             frequency="monthly", transform="level",
                             partial_period="exclude")
        except Exception:
            continue
        if df is not None and len(df) > 0:
            got = (df, measure)
            break
    if got is None:
        raise RuntimeError("no monthly level series returned for %s" % code)
    df, measure = got
    measure_used[code] = measure
    idx = pd.to_datetime(df["date"]).dt.to_period("M")
    ser = pd.Series(np.asarray(df["value"], dtype=float), index=idx)
    levels[code] = ser.reindex(grid)          # missing natural months -> NaN (kept)

print("measure used:", measure_used)
print("grid months: %d (2018-12..2025-12), analysis months: %d (2019-01..2025-12)"
      % (len(grid), len(analysis)))

# ---- monthly returns on the grid: only contiguous adjacent months ----------
rets = {}
for code in CODES:
    lv = levels[code]
    prev = lv.shift(1)
    ok = lv.notna() & prev.notna()
    rets[code] = (lv / prev - 1.0).where(ok)

# ---- per-asset cross-sample facts -----------------------------------------
rows_assets, audit_assets = [], []
for code in CODES:
    present = levels[code].notna()
    r = rets[code].reindex(analysis).dropna()
    n_price = int(present.sum())
    n_missing = int(len(grid) - n_price)
    n_ret = int(len(r))
    vol = float(r.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(12)) if n_ret > 1 else float("nan")
    q25, q50, q75 = (np.quantile(r.to_numpy(float), [0.25, 0.50, 0.75]) if n_ret > 0
                     else (np.nan, np.nan, np.nan))
    gaps = [str(p) for p in grid[~present]]
    rows_assets.append({
        "asset": "%s (%s)" % (ROLE[code], code), "measure": measure_used[code],
        "price_rows": n_price, "missing_months": n_missing, "valid_returns": n_ret,
        "annual_vol": vol, "q25": float(q25), "q50": float(q50), "q75": float(q75),
        "missing_list": ",".join(gaps) if gaps else "-",
    })
    audit_assets.append({
        "asset": code, "price_rows": n_price, "missing_months": n_missing,
        "valid_returns": n_ret, "annual_vol": finite_or_none(vol),
        "q25": finite_or_none(q25), "q50": finite_or_none(q50), "q75": finite_or_none(q75),
    })

asset_tbl = pd.DataFrame(rows_assets)
print("\n[Asset sample facts] monthly returns are decimal fractions (0.01 = 1%)")
print(asset_tbl.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: "%.6f" % v))

# ---- paired complete-sample analysis (A-B and A-C) -------------------------
PERIODS = [("all", analysis), ("pre2023", mask_pre), ("post2023", mask_post)]
PAIRS = [("000300.SH", "000852.SH"), ("000300.SH", "000905.SH")]

def pair_block(xr, yr, mask):
    m = mask & xr.notna() & yr.notna()
    x = xr.reindex(mask).where(m, np.nan).dropna().to_numpy(float)
    y = yr.reindex(mask).where(m, np.nan).dropna().to_numpy(float)
    n = int(len(x))
    if n < 3:
        return {"n": n, "pearson": None, "spearman": None,
                "alpha_monthly": None, "beta": None}
    pear = float(stats.pearsonr(x, y)[0])
    spear = float(stats.spearmanr(x, y)[0])
    fit = sm.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(x)).fit()
    return {"n": n, "pearson": pear, "spearman": spear,
            "alpha_monthly": float(fit.params[0]), "beta": float(fit.params[1])}

rows_pairs, audit_pairs = [], []
for xcode, ycode in PAIRS:
    xr, yr = rets[xcode], rets[ycode]
    for pname, mask in PERIODS:
        b = pair_block(xr, yr, mask)
        rows_pairs.append({
            "pair": "%s / %s" % (xcode, ycode), "y": ROLE[ycode], "period": pname,
            "n": b["n"], "pearson": b["pearson"], "spearman": b["spearman"],
            "alpha_monthly": b["alpha_monthly"], "beta": b["beta"],
        })
        audit_pairs.append({
            "pair": "%s/%s" % (xcode, ycode), "period": pname, "n": b["n"],
            "pearson": finite_or_none(b["pearson"]),
            "spearman": finite_or_none(b["spearman"]),
            "alpha_monthly": finite_or_none(b["alpha_monthly"]),
            "beta": finite_or_none(b["beta"]),
        })

pair_tbl = pd.DataFrame(rows_pairs)
print("\n[Paired complete-sample stats] y = B or C, x = A; alpha per month (decimal), no rounding applied")
print(pair_tbl.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: "%.6f" % v))

# ---- rolling 12-month correlation, gaps preserved --------------------------
def rolling_corr(x, y, win=WIN):
    out = pd.Series(np.nan, index=grid, dtype=float)
    for i in range(win, len(grid)):
        wx, wy = x.iloc[i - win + 1:i + 1], y.iloc[i - win + 1:i + 1]
        if wx.notna().all() and wy.notna().all():
            out.iloc[i] = float(np.corrcoef(wx.to_numpy(float), wy.to_numpy(float))[0, 1])
    return out

rc = {
    "A-B": rolling_corr(rets["000300.SH"], rets["000852.SH"]),
    "A-C": rolling_corr(rets["000300.SH"], rets["000905.SH"]),
}
for k, s in rc.items():
    v = s.dropna()
    print("\n[Rolling 12-month corr %s] valid windows=%d, span=%s..%s, min=%.4f, max=%.4f"
          % (k, len(v), (v.index.min() if len(v) else "-"), (v.index.max() if len(v) else "-"),
             (v.min() if len(v) else float("nan")), (v.max() if len(v) else float("nan"))))

# ---- figures (Matplotlib, English labels; NaN breaks the line) -------------
x_dates = grid.to_timestamp(how="end")
base_month = grid[0]
for p in grid:
    if all(levels[c].notna().loc[p] for c in CODES):
        base_month = p
        break
split = pd.Timestamp("2023-01-31")

fig1, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.5))
for code in CODES:
    norm = levels[code] / levels[code].loc[base_month] * 100.0
    ax1.plot(x_dates, norm.to_numpy(float), lw=1.6, label=LABEL[code])
ax1.axvline(split, color="0.35", ls="--", lw=1.0)
ax1.text(split, ax1.get_ylim()[1], " 2023-01 split", va="top", ha="left", fontsize=9, color="0.3")
ax1.set_title("Month-end index level, rebased to 100 at %s (synthetic data, CNY)" % base_month)
ax1.set_xlabel("Month end"); ax1.set_ylabel("Rebased level (start = 100)")
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3); ax1.legend(loc="upper left")
ax1.text(0.01, 0.02, "Gaps in a line = missing month-end observation (not filled)",
         transform=ax1.transAxes, fontsize=8, color="0.3")
fig1.tight_layout()

fig2, ax2 = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5.0))
for k, s in rc.items():
    ax2.plot(s.index.to_timestamp(how="end"), s.to_numpy(float), lw=1.6, label="Rolling 12M corr %s" % k)
ax2.axhline(0.0, color="0.6", lw=0.9)
ax2.axvline(split, color="0.35", ls="--", lw=1.0)
ax2.set_ylim(-1.05, 1.05)
ax2.set_title("Rolling correlation of monthly returns (window = 12 consecutive calendar months)")
ax2.set_xlabel("Window end (month end)"); ax2.set_ylabel("Pearson correlation")
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3); ax2.legend(loc="lower left")
ax2.text(0.01, 0.02, "Defined only where all 12 paired monthly observations are complete; "
                     "gaps = missing month or insufficient window",
         transform=ax2.transAxes, fontsize=8, color="0.3")
fig2.tight_layout()

print("\n[Reading note] A 12-month window is 12 consecutive calendar months with 12 complete "
      "paired returns; a cleaned 12-return subset spanning fewer months is never labelled as 12 months.")

audit = {"assets": audit_assets, "pairs": audit_pairs}
print("AUDIT_JSON=" + json.dumps(audit, ensure_ascii=False))

ax2.set_xlabel("Window end (month end)"); ax2.set_ylabel("Pearson correlation")

inputScope: Synthetic demo data in the isolated library: three CNY month-end index price-level series identified only as A=000300.SH, B=000852.SH, C=000905.SH. Loaded with data.series("index", code, start="20181201", end="20251231", measure="market.adjusted_close", frequency="monthly", transform="level", partial_period="exclude"); for a price index this measure returns the index level itself. The CNY-benchmark-relative measure market.cny_close is not applicable to these codes (it is restricted to registered cross-market benchmarks), so it is not used. 2018-12 is the warm-up month for the first return; the analysis window is 2019-01..2025-12 (84 months) on a complete natural-month grid of 85 months. Missing months stay NaN: no forward fill, no zero fill, and no return is computed across a missing month. Annualized volatility = sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of monthly returns x sqrt(12). Quantiles use numpy linear interpolation. Pair analysis uses only months where both assets have a valid single-month return; OLS is y=B or C on x=A with intercept (statsmodels), alpha in decimal per month. Rolling correlation uses 12 consecutive calendar-month returns and stays undefined unless all 12 paired observations are complete. These are price indices (no dividends, not tradable), the window is short, and the data are explicitly synthetic, so nothing here is a validated investment conclusion. The prior run (revision 1) failed on a shape mismatch in the paired mask; only the mask construction changed.
